summary.text: St. Aaron, elder brother of St. Moses, serves as his spokesman and becomes the priest associated with Israel’s sanctuary worship.
summary.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

saints.context: The source’s received ecclesiastical narrative is identified as such. Uncertain dates, later traditions and unknown circumstances of death are retained as uncertain.

blocks.text: Exodus identifies St. Aaron as the elder brother of St. Moses and appoints him to speak alongside Moses before the people and Pharaoh. His story belongs to Israel’s deliverance from slavery and the journey through the wilderness.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: St. Aaron shares in the confrontation with Pharaoh and supports Moses during the battle against Amalek. God appoints him and his sons for priestly service connected with the tabernacle, the movable sanctuary. Scripture also records his involvement in making the golden calf and his need for correction. The account therefore includes both divine calling and serious human failure.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: Numbers recounts the transfer of his priestly garments to his son on Mount Hor and Aaron’s death there. A later passage gives his age as 123. The text describes death during the wilderness journey, not martyrdom.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The OCA explicitly names St. Aaron as a righteous priest among the Forefathers. Its account relates his work with St. Moses to the Exodus narrative.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: Hebrews uses Aaron’s divine calling when explaining priesthood, then develops its teaching about Christ’s high priesthood. This comparison distinguishes the older priestly ministry from Christ’s definitive work.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

death.label: Death on Mount Hor at 123 in Numbers; no martyrdom described
